recipes.name: Feta Cheese Turkey Burgers
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup kalamata olives, pitted and sliced

steps.text: Preheat the grill to medium-high heat.
Combine turkey, feta cheese, olives, oregano, and pepper in a large bowl. Mix together, and form into patties.
Lightly oil the grate. Place patties on the grill. Cook for 10 to 12 minutes, turning halfway through.

raw_recipe.headline: Feta Cheese Turkey Burgers
raw_recipe.description: Move over hamburgers, this turkey burger recipe is studded with feta cheese, Kalamata olives, and oregano. Grill and serve for a fabulous meal.
raw_recipe.name: Feta Cheese Turkey Burgers

review.reviewBody: Good Lord Almight! These burgers are fantastic! After blending the ingredients, I let them set up in the fridge for about 1 hour before forming patties. Grilling was no problem after brushing the grill with a generous layer of olive oil. Forget the bun -- these burgers don't need it. Instead top with a layer of steamed spinich and serve with Sweet potato french fries. Visually stunning and absolutely delicious!!

So moist! I added a tsp of pesto and used Greek spice instead of oregano. Since I did not have any olives on hand, I used Sun Dried Tomatoes instead. Fried them in a cast iron skillet and served on homemade toasted bread. Moist and tasty! A keeper!

Very very tasty... But I made a taste change right at the start. Instead of oregano, I used Turkish Seasoning from Penzey's Spices. I also made a yogurt sauce of plain yogurt and a little of the Turkish mix. I discovered that the feta in the turkey mix starts to burn before the turkey was done, so I plan to play with perhaps adding less to the turkey mix and putting some on top, like a cheeseburger. Will definitely keep this in the mix of meals

These were fantastic! I used lean ground turkey and jumbo black olives, from a can I sliced, that worked fine. The 1 cup of feta ended up being near a 6 oz package. I used leveled spoons of the oregano and just a couple lite sprinkles of black pepper. I shaped the patties using a mashed potato scoop and got 7. I decided to cook them in the house in a pan sprayed with olive oil, but they didn't seem to be getting as brown as I liked. So, I lined a sheet with foil and finished them under the broiler for 2 minutes on each side. That made them perfect. I ate on a wheat but with a little lite mayo, leaf lettuce, sliced tomatoe and onion. I wish feta cheese hadn't gotten so expensive. This makes a great lunch!

These are the best ever. Have made them several times over the summer. I use regular sliced black olives as that is what is available around here. Still they taste great. After making up the patties I freeze them and when ready to BBQ put them on the grill frozen. They stay together beautifully and come off the grill moist on the inside and well grilled on the outside. Last time we cooked them over an open campfire. The added smokey flavor was to die for. Thanks for a great recipe.

This is great!! Granted I did change it a little based off some reviews I read. I added 1/3 cup dried oatmeal (instead of breadcrumbs) and 1 egg to hold it together. I also added some Greek Seasoning with the oregano and about 1 tsp worcestershire sauce. I put it on the george foreman grill for about 15 minutes and they came out perfect! They werent dry at all!

This is a new favorite for my family. It's very quick and easy to make. Mix in a 4 oz container of flavored crumbled feta to the ground turkey. We like the tomato basil flavor. We don't use the olives or oregano. Form your patties and season with a little pepper, and that's it. I fry them up in a cast iron pan. What really makes it special is using roasted red peppers and baby spinach for your toppings, instead of tomato and lettuce. Really good!

These were delicious!!! I read a lot of the reviews. I followed the recipe exactly but the additions I made were 1 tsp of mediterranean seasoning, a bit of olive oil infused with garlic and 2 tsp. of Balsamic Vinegar. I also cooked them on top of the stove and it took @ 10-12 minutes. I served them with a recipe I found on this sight : 1/2 cup of greek non fat yogurt, 2 TBS mayo, 2 tsp. dried Italian seasonng, garlic powder and some fresh lemon juice. This recipe made 5 burgers. They were very moist and not dry. I did mix it up and let it sit in the fridge for @ 45 minutes and then made into patties. Delicious!! This is a keeper.

These are absolutely great. I made these tonight. Like a prior reviewer, I added garlic to the mix. I placed all the ingredients in a large zip loc bag and smushed it all together and let it sit for a couple of hours in the fridge. Patties were great with a little Frank's Red Hot on a whole wheat pita. Spinach, roasted red peppers, it's all good! Excellent warmed up, too for a quick lunch.

To this recipe, I add 1 tsp lemon zest, 1/2 cup chopped fresh baby spinach, and 1/4 cup chopped red onion. The result is fabulous. I serve with a tomato slice and store-bought tzatziki sauce (Cedar's) on flatouts or small wheat pitas.

Nice flavor that most anyone wold enjoy. Added 1/4 cup chicken broth, 1/4 tsp pepper & 1/2 tsp salt and reduced kalamata olives somewhat to limit the fat content. Cooked on George Foreman grill for 5 minutes. Served on toasted bun with homemade tzatziki sauce, spring mix greens & fresh tomatoes. Welcome change from the traditional burger...would be awesome with a greek salad (tomatoes, feta, fresh basil & oregano, onions & olives). Definitely worth a try!
Really good. Unique taste, But absolutely delicious!

I have made this recipe for years. Love the flavors. The saltiness of the feta and the tanginess of the olives hits all the flavor profiles in your mouth. Every once in a while I make add some chopped pickled jalapenos for a spicy kick.
I love olives and it was delicious
Not bad. Moist but a bit bland.
Awesome recipe however tonight I had no feta cheese so used a Mexican blend cheese instead - and what a great turkey burger. I served with blue cheese dressing and got 5 stars from hubby !
I like this recipe and cut up a left over patty and put it on home made pizza. It was real good.
These were pretty good. I made them exactly as written except cooked on high instead of medium high. Not sure if I will make them again, but perhaps. Thank you for the recipe!

I’ve made these twice now. Once on the grill and once in my cast-iron skillet. I followed the recipe exactly except the one change I made was I added Mediterranean season instead of only oregano. These turned out fantastic both times! I serve them on a whole wheat bun with mozzarella cheese, pickles, and homemade Tzatziki sauce. No leftovers to speak of!
Delicious. Added garlic powder and very little salt. Sautéed on skillet w/ olive oil and game out great. I have no grill. Husband ate two burger
